calc.title: Risk Calculator
calc.subtitle: Answer a few questions to discover your risk profile and get personalized strategy recommendations.
calc.start_exploring_desc: Based on your profile, these categories are your best starting points. Dive in and discover strategies that match your risk level.
calc.income: What is your monthly income range?
calc.savings: How much do you have in savings/emergency fund?
calc.risk_tolerance: How would you describe your risk tolerance?
calc.time_horizon: What is your investment time horizon?
calc.goals: What are your primary financial goals?
calc.advice.conservative.desc: You value safety and stability above all. That's not a weakness — it's a foundation. Your priority is protecting what you have while slowly building more. The good news: the safest strategies are also the most proven over time.
calc.advice.conservative.action1: Open a high-yield savings account today and set up an automatic transfer of even $25/week — this builds the habit that matters more than the amount
calc.advice.conservative.action2: Calculate your emergency fund target (3-6 months of expenses) and write it on a sticky note where you see it daily
calc.advice.conservative.action3: Read about the 50/30/20 budgeting rule — knowing where your money goes is the first step to controlling it
calc.advice.conservative.experiment: Put $50 in a separate envelope or account. Don't touch it for 30 days. At the end, notice how it feels to have that small safety net. That feeling is the seed of financial confidence.
calc.advice.moderate.desc: You're careful but open to growth. This is actually the sweet spot for long-term wealth building — you have the patience to let compound interest work, and the courage to put your money somewhere it can grow.
calc.advice.moderate.action1: Set up a brokerage account and buy your first index fund (even $100 is enough to start) — the hardest part is the first purchase
calc.advice.moderate.action2: Automate a monthly investment of a fixed amount — even $50/month at 8% return becomes $35,000 in 20 years
calc.advice.moderate.action3: Learn about dollar cost averaging — it removes the stress of 'timing the market' and turns investing into a simple routine
calc.advice.moderate.experiment: Split $100 into two: put $50 in a savings account and $50 in a broad index fund (like an S&P 500 ETF). Check both after 6 months. See the difference between saving and investing with your own eyes.
calc.advice.balanced.desc: You understand that some risk is necessary for growth, but you want to sleep well at night. You're the type who can build real wealth over time because you won't panic-sell during dips, but you also won't leave all your money under the mattress.
calc.advice.balanced.action1: Build a simple 3-fund portfolio: domestic stocks, international stocks, and bonds — this gives you diversification with minimal effort
calc.advice.balanced.action2: Identify one skill you could monetize as a side income (freelancing, consulting, digital products) and take the first step this week
calc.advice.balanced.action3: Review your subscriptions and recurring expenses — redirect what you save into your investment account
calc.advice.balanced.experiment: Take $200 and split it three ways: $100 in index funds, $50 in a slightly riskier investment (a sector ETF or REIT), and $50 in learning (a book or online course about investing). Track all three for 6 months — you'll learn what kind of investor you naturally are.
calc.advice.growth.desc: You're ambitious and willing to accept volatility for higher returns. You have the temperament to handle market swings — just make sure you have a solid foundation first. The biggest risk for growth-oriented investors isn't the market — it's overconfidence.
calc.advice.growth.action1: Make sure you have at least 3 months of emergency savings BEFORE taking on higher-risk investments — this prevents forced selling during downturns
calc.advice.growth.action2: Allocate no more than 10-20% of your portfolio to high-risk/high-reward strategies — keep the core in proven index funds
calc.advice.growth.action3: Start building a second income stream — your job funds your life, your side income funds your investments
calc.advice.growth.experiment: Set aside $500. Put $300 in a growth ETF, and $200 in a single stock you've researched thoroughly. Track both for 3 months. Compare your stock-picking results to the ETF — most professionals can't beat the index, and this experiment will teach you why diversification matters.
calc.advice.aggressive.desc: You're a risk-taker who sees opportunity where others see danger. This can lead to exceptional returns — or exceptional losses. The key difference between successful aggressive investors and gamblers is research, discipline, and knowing exactly how much you can afford to lose.
calc.advice.aggressive.action1: Set a hard loss limit BEFORE you invest: 'I will not risk more than X% of my total savings on high-risk plays' — write it down and stick to it
calc.advice.aggressive.action2: Build your knowledge base first: learn to read financial statements, understand market cycles, and study at least 3 strategies before committing real money
calc.advice.aggressive.action3: Paper-trade (simulate) your strategy for 30 days before using real money — this tests your approach without the emotional pressure
calc.advice.aggressive.experiment: Take $100 you can afford to lose completely. Use it to try one high-risk strategy (crypto, options, individual stock). Track every decision and emotion in a journal for 30 days. Win or lose, the journal is worth more than the investment — it shows you your real risk tolerance, not the one you imagined.

principle.pay_yourself_first.desc: Before paying bills or spending, set aside a portion of your income for savings and investments.
principle.pay_yourself_first.quote: Do not save what is left after spending, but spend what is left after saving. — Warren Buffett
principle.pay_yourself_first.explanation: Treat savings as a non-negotiable expense. Automate transfers to savings/investment accounts on payday. Even 10% consistently invested will compound dramatically over decades.
principle.compound_interest.desc: Earning returns on your returns — the most powerful force in wealth building.
principle.compound_interest.quote: Compound interest is the eighth wonder of the world. He who understands it, earns it; he who doesn't, pays it. — Albert Einstein
principle.compound_interest.explanation: A $10,000 investment growing at 7% annually becomes $76,123 in 30 years without adding a single dollar. Start early — time is the key ingredient.
principle.diversification.desc: Don't put all your eggs in one basket. Spread risk across different assets, sectors, and geographies.
principle.diversification.quote: Diversification is the only free lunch in investing. — Harry Markowitz
principle.diversification.explanation: When one investment drops, others may hold or rise. A diversified portfolio reduces volatility without necessarily reducing returns.
principle.risk_reward.desc: Higher potential returns always come with higher risk. There are no exceptions.
principle.risk_reward.quote: Risk is what's left over when you think you've thought of everything. — Carl Richards
principle.risk_reward.explanation: If someone promises high returns with no risk, they're either lying or don't understand risk. Always ask: what can go wrong, and can I afford to lose this?
principle.emergency_fund.desc: Before investing, build 3-6 months of living expenses in a liquid, accessible account.
principle.emergency_fund.quote: An emergency fund turns a crisis into an inconvenience.
principle.emergency_fund.explanation: Without an emergency fund, any unexpected expense forces you to sell investments at the worst time or take on high-interest debt.
principle.dollar_cost_averaging.desc: Invest a fixed amount at regular intervals regardless of market conditions.
principle.dollar_cost_averaging.quote: The best time to invest was yesterday. The second best time is today.
principle.dollar_cost_averaging.explanat: By investing consistently, you buy more shares when prices are low and fewer when high. This eliminates the need to time the market — which even professionals fail at.
principle.live_below_means.desc: Spend less than you earn. The gap between income and expenses is your wealth-building engine.
principle.live_below_means.quote: It's not your salary that makes you rich, it's your spending habits. — Charles A. Jaffe
principle.live_below_means.explanation: Wealth is not about income — it's about the difference between what you earn and what you spend. Many high earners are broke because they spend it all.
principle.time_in_market: Time in Market vs. Timing the Market
principle.time_in_market.desc: Staying invested consistently beats trying to predict market highs and lows.
principle.time_in_market.quote: Far more money has been lost by investors trying to anticipate corrections than has been lost in the corrections themselves. — Peter Lynch
principle.time_in_market.explanation: Missing just the 10 best trading days over 20 years can cut your returns in half. Stay invested, stay patient.
principle.asset_allocation.desc: How you divide your money between stocks, bonds, real estate, and cash matters more than which specific investments you pick.
principle.asset_allocation.quote: Asset allocation determines about 90% of portfolio return variability. — Brinson, Hood & Beebower
principle.asset_allocation.explanation: A well-balanced portfolio aligned with your age, goals, and risk tolerance is the single most important investment decision you'll make.
principle.tax_efficiency.desc: It's not what you earn — it's what you keep after taxes.
principle.tax_efficiency.quote: The avoidance of taxes is the only intellectual pursuit that carries any reward. — John Maynard Keynes
principle.tax_efficiency.explanation: Use tax-advantaged accounts (401k, IRA, Roth). Understand capital gains vs. income tax. Tax-loss harvesting can offset gains. Small tax savings compound enormously.
principle.debt_management.desc: Attack high-interest debt aggressively. Debt is the opposite of compound interest — it works against you.
principle.debt_management.quote: The borrower is slave to the lender. — Proverbs 22:7
principle.debt_management.explanation: Avalanche: pay highest interest first (saves most money). Snowball: pay smallest balance first (builds momentum). Both work — pick what keeps you motivated.
principle.multiple_streams.desc: Don't rely on a single source of income. Build multiple streams for security and growth.
principle.multiple_streams.quote: Never depend on a single income. Make investments to create a second source. — Warren Buffett
principle.multiple_streams.explanation: The average millionaire has 7 income streams. Start with your job, add investments, then a side hustle. Each stream adds both income and security.
